business_problem: The 75th U.S. Army Reserve Innovation Command wanted to modernize administrative and planning work and give military police teams better ways to collect and analyze checkpoint footage and other surveillance, while proving that technical Soldiers could deliver useful operational AI capabilities faster than traditional acquisition processes.
solution_summary: The 75th U.S. Army Reserve Innovation Command, through its Army Applications Group, ran a two-week code-a-thon to build in-house AI applications inside a secure, open-internet development environment with access to commercial-grade AI models. The team developed and rehearsed several prototypes tied to concrete Army workflows: MP Sentinel-Video RAG, described as a novel multimodal Video RAG engine for military police tactical operations; a TA-50 computer vision application to reduce the inventory burden; and a Soldier Passport system to streamline administrative readiness. The implementation paired software engineers, product managers, data scientists, and military domain experts in an agile sprint, then moved the prototypes from development into operational demonstration during Operation Sentinel Justice 26, where senior leaders reviewed how the tools could support security analysis, readiness, and mission execution.

solution_components.role: AAG's multimodal retrieval-augmented generation prototype analyzes checkpoint footage and other surveillance to support military police tactical operations.

solution_components.name: TA-50 computer vision application
solution_components.role: This prototype applies computer vision to TA-50 inventory workflows to reduce inventory burden and system overload.

solution_components.name: Soldier Passport system
solution_components.role: This system streamlines administrative readiness tasks for Soldiers and unit operations.

data_flow: For MP Sentinel-Video RAG, checkpoint footage and other critical site surveillance are taken from operational sources, processed by the multimodal Video RAG prototype for retrieval and AI-assisted analysis, and then surfaced to military police security teams and senior leaders as operational insight during OSJ 26 demonstrations. Parallel prototypes feed inventory and readiness workflows for TA-50 and Soldier Passport use cases.
business_outcome: The command produced several working AI prototypes, demonstrated that Soldiers could build and operationalize advanced AI models quickly, and showed leaders how AI tools could improve efficiency, accuracy, readiness, and surveillance analysis in Army operations.
